comments.body:
Scope correction and a conflict the fix must resolve deliberately, both found within the hour of filing.

**It is FOUR call sites, not three.** Epic 6202's S5 merged as `8629e3874aea` while I was writing this ticket and added a fourth consumer of `pct_of_cap`:

    --value "$(pct_of_cap "$docker_container_bytes" "$CONTAINER_WRITABLE_BYTES")"

So the affected set is now `docker_storage_used_percent`, `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent`, `journal_used_percent`, and the new container writable-layer percentage. The defect is spreading by ordinary reuse, which is the expected behaviour of a shared helper and is an argument for fixing the helper rather than the call sites.

**The conflict: S5's acceptance criteria REQUIRE the clamp.** Ticket `910b-2d43-4482-4c64` AC3 reads, in part, *"percent clamped to 100"* — clamping is written into a criterion that is being verified right now, and there is very likely a test pinning it. So this ticket and that one currently disagree about whether clamping is correct behaviour.

I am deliberately NOT resolving that by intervening in S5's verification. Its AC describes what was built, the verifier's job is to confirm the built thing matches, and having it verify against a criterion I have just contradicted would corrupt a close that is otherwise sound. S5 should close as written.

**What that means for whoever fixes this ticket.** The change is not "delete two lines from `pct_of_cap`". It must:

1. Change the helper, then find and update the test(s) that pin clamping — at minimum S5's, and any equivalent for the older three metrics.
2. Amend S5's AC3 language, or record on that ticket that the criterion was superseded. A closed ticket carrying a criterion that the tree no longer satisfies is its own future confusion, and this is exactly the shape of defect that `affd-913c-3fb0-40fb` was about: a contract that existed only inside one commit and silently disappeared.
3. Re-check the four alarms' thresholds. A metric that could never exceed 100 can now do so; confirm no alarm relied on the ceiling.

**Do not read the conflict as evidence the clamp is fine.** S5's AC was written before the live overshoot was measured, and specifying a clamp is a reasonable-looking choice until you see a 5.875 GB cache against a 5.00 GiB budget publishing 100. The measurement postdates the criterion.

**Sequencing.** This ticket should not be dispatched until S5's close lands, or the two will fight over the same function and the same tests in overlapping worktrees.

comments.body:
**Scope correction: it is FIVE call sites on current `origin/main`, not three or four.** The ticket names three and the follow-up comment adds the container writable layer as a fourth. `/var/tmp` is the fifth — `var_tmp_used_percent` (§2h, story `2ba3`) derives through the same helper. The complete set:

| metric | cap | §  |
|---|---|---|
| `docker_storage_used_percent` | `DOCKER_BUDGET_BYTES` | 2f |
| `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` | `DOCKER_BUILDKIT_CACHE_BYTES` | 2f |
| `journal_used_percent` | `JOURNAL_MAX_USE_BYTES` | 2g |
| `var_tmp_used_percent` | `VAR_TMP_MAX_BYTES` | 2h |
| `container_writable_used_percent` | `CONTAINER_WRITABLE_BYTES` | 2i |

The defect spreading by ordinary reuse — three sites at filing, five a day later — is itself the argument for fixing the helper rather than the sites, which is what this change does.

**Fix.** `pct_of_cap` is now `printf '%s\n' "$(( $1 * 100 / $2 ))"` with no upper bound, and its comment states why a BUDGET ratio must be able to exceed 100 where a fill-level gauge need not.

**RED before GREEN.** New `tests/scripts/test_observability_pct_of_cap_b380.py` drives the shipped function definition (lifted out by text — the script is a straight-line probe that cannot be sourced) and failed on the pre-fix tree with `assert 100 == 109` at the live production numbers, plus 150/300/1000 and a structural no-upper-bound guard. The four existing end-to-end clamp tests were rewritten to assert true ratios and each failed for the same reason first: journal `assert 100 == 200`, var_tmp `assert 100 == 225`, container `assert 100 == 300`, docker `assert 100 == 300`. All 65 tests across the five files pass after the fix.

**Seeded-defect proof.** Re-introducing a clamp at ONE call site only (the BuildKit `--value` expression, leaving the shared helper honest) turns `test_a_budget_overrun_publishes_its_true_ratio` RED with `assert 100 == 240`. A future clamp re-introduced at any single site is caught. Reverted.

**Consumer sweep — five alarms, no dashboards, one doc.** All five percentages are consumed by exactly one alarm each in `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf`: `rebar-docker-storage-cap-high` (407), `rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` (446), `rebar-journal-usage-high` (562), `rebar-var-tmp-usage-high` (655), `rebar-container-writable-usage-high` (750). **Every one is `GreaterThanThreshold` at `threshold = 85`, `statistic = "Maximum"`, `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`.** No alarm on any of these metrics uses `LessThanThreshold`, a band, an upper bound, anomaly detection or a math expression — the only `LessThanThreshold`/`threshold = 1` alarms in the file watch the 1/0 heartbeat metrics (`container_reaper_active`, `journal_cap_in_effect`, `var_tmp_cleanup_active`, `mcp_healthy`), none of which touch `pct_of_cap`. **No threshold and no unit needs changing:** a value that was clamped to 100 already breached 85, so every datapoint that fired before still fires, and unclamping strictly WIDENS what these alarms can distinguish rather than changing when they trip. CloudWatch's `Percent` unit is a label on a double, not a validated range, so 109 and 300 are accepted datapoints. There are **no `aws_cloudwatch_dashboard` resources in the repo at all**, so the "rescales a shared axis" argument in the original clamp comment had no actual consumer to protect. `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` gained a paragraph telling an operator that a reading above 100 is real and how far past the cap it means, and the BuildKit alarm row now reads "at, or PAST, its own cap".

**S5 conflict.** Recorded as a comment on `910b-2d43-4482-4c64` (`francium-written-squid`) rather than by editing a closed ticket's description: AC3's "percent clamped to 100" is superseded, with the measurement that postdates it and a restatement of how AC3 should now be read. Its four other guarantees are untouched.

**AC4 (re-measure live) is NOT satisfiable and is deliberately not claimed.** The reporting session pruned that build cache after filing; it reads 0 now, and this agent is barred from mutating the production host. The equivalent proof is the unit test at the exact recorded numbers (5 875 000 000 B against 5 GiB → 109), which is reproducible where the live host is not.

comments.body:
Two notes from the reporting session, one of them an admission.

**AC4 is currently unverifiable BECAUSE OF ME, and I should have foreseen it.** That criterion asks for the live BuildKit overshoot to be re-measured after the fix. It cannot be, because I pruned that cache at ~10:55 UTC while relieving disk pressure on the host — `docker builder prune -f`, 5.877 GB, 0 active entries. The overshoot this ticket was filed on no longer exists to re-measure.

I filed this ticket at ~09:30 with the overshoot as its centrepiece, then destroyed the reproduction about ninety minutes later for an unrelated and defensible reason, without noticing the two touched. The prune was still the right call on its own merits — the reclaim floor was rising and the cache was 100% reclaimable — but "does this remove evidence a ticket depends on?" is a question I did not ask and should have.

So AC4 as written asks for something the tree can no longer produce on demand. The substitute the implementing agent recorded is sound and I endorse it: `pct_of_cap 5875000000 5368709120` -> 109, a unit test at the exact bytes I measured live, which is reproducible where the host no longer is. That is arguably a BETTER artifact than the original criterion asked for, since it does not depend on catching the host in a particular state. Whoever closes this should either accept that substitution explicitly or mark AC4 `[non-codebase]` and record the live confirmation when the next natural overshoot occurs — but it should not sit open waiting for a condition I removed.

**The scope grew again, and the pattern is the argument for the fix that was chosen.** Call sites were THREE when I filed, FOUR when I briefed (S5's container metric, commit `8629e3874aea`), and **FIVE** on the current tree — `var_tmp_used_percent` against `VAR_TMP_MAX_BYTES`, from story `2ba3`, which nobody had counted including me. Every one arrived by ordinary reuse of a shared helper. That is exactly why fixing `pct_of_cap` rather than the call sites is right: the site count is a moving target and the helper is not.

Worth recording plainly: the original clamp's stated justification was that "a datapoint of 300 rescales every dashboard that shares the axis". The sweep found **no `aws_cloudwatch_dashboard` resource anywhere in the repo**. The clamp was protecting a consumer that does not exist, at the cost of blinding five cap-compliance metrics to the one condition they are deployed to detect.

**One more caveat on the local evidence, since the report is honest about it and I do not want it lost.** `make verify` did not come back green on that tree: 29 failed, of which **26 were `GateCongestedError` — the host's four-slot gate-admission semaphore saturated by other agents I had running concurrently on the same box**. Zero failures in any touched file, and the targeted 81-test run across all five observability files is clean. That congestion is my orchestration cost, not a property of this change, and it is `stuffed-energistic-ladybird`'s subject.

comments.body:
**Landed. Gerrit 2679 merged as `d6669496cae4`, now the tip of `origin/main`** (double-green: `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1`, submitted by the operator). Change: `pct_of_cap` no longer clamps; five metrics, five tests, one runbook paragraph.

## AC verdicts

**AC1 — the helper no longer clamps: MET.** `infra/scripts/observability.sh` now reads

    pct_of_cap() {
      printf '%s\n' "$(( $1 * 100 / $2 ))"
    }

Proven by `tests/scripts/test_observability_pct_of_cap_b380.py`, which drives the SHIPPED function definition (lifted out by text — the script is a straight-line probe that cannot be sourced). Over-cap at the live numbers returns 109; exactly at the cap returns 100, so no off-by-one was introduced. RED first on the pre-fix tree with `assert 100 == 109`.

**AC2 — every call site publishes unclamped, and a re-introduced clamp is caught: MET, over FIVE sites not three.** The ticket named three; the follow-up comment added the container writable layer as a fourth; `var_tmp_used_percent` (§2h, story `2ba3`) is the fifth and nobody had counted it. All five are covered by construction because the fix is in the shared helper. Each has an end-to-end over-cap test asserting its true ratio — docker 300, buildkit 240, journal 200, var_tmp 225, container 300 — and each was RED first with `assert 100 == <that value>`.

The "future re-introduction at any single site is caught" half is proven by seeding, not asserted. Re-introducing a clamp at ONE call site only (wrapping the BuildKit `--value` expression, leaving the shared helper honest) turned `test_a_budget_overrun_publishes_its_true_ratio` RED with **`assert 100 == 240`**. In the SAME run `test_storage_and_buildkit_are_published_against_their_own_caps` — an at-cap input expecting exactly 100 — **passed with the clamp seeded**. That contrast is the point: only an over-cap assertion can discriminate, and a proof built on under-cap inputs would have been vacuous, which would be a poor way to verify the fix for a vacuous-check bug. Seed reverted; `git diff` confirmed only the intended change remained. A `2 GiB + 1` case pins the floor-division boundary so a future clamp cannot hide behind it.

**AC3 — checked against every consumer, with an explicit statement: MET. No alarm threshold and no unit needs changing.** All five percentages feed exactly one alarm each, all in `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`: `rebar-docker-storage-cap-high` (407), `rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` (446), `rebar-journal-usage-high` (562), `rebar-var-tmp-usage-high` (655), `rebar-container-writable-usage-high` (750). Every one is `GreaterThanThreshold`, `threshold = 85`, `statistic = "Maximum"`, `treat_missing_data = "breaching"`, 300/3/2. **A datapoint clamped to 100 already breached 85**, so every datapoint that fired before still fires — unclamping cannot make an alarm stop firing, it only widens what the alarm can tell apart. No alarm on these five uses `LessThanThreshold`, a band, an upper bound, anomaly detection or metric math; the `LessThanThreshold`/`threshold = 1` alarms in that file (342, 609, 702, 798) watch the 1/0 heartbeats, none of which touch `pct_of_cap`. `monitoring.tf` references only `disk_used_percent` / `root_disk_used_percent`, published by paths that never call the helper. **There are no `aws_cloudwatch_dashboard` resources in the repo at all** — so "a datapoint of 300 rescales every dashboard that shares the axis", the original clamp's stated justification, had no consumer to protect. CloudWatch's `Percent` unit is a label on a double, not a validated range, so 109 and 300 are accepted datapoints and `--unit Percent` stays. No `.tf` file was modified and no `terraform apply` was run. `tests/unit/test_alarm_actions_terraform.py` passes unchanged. `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md` gained a paragraph telling an operator a reading above 100 is real and how far past the cap it means, and the BuildKit alarm row now reads "at, or PAST, its own cap".

**AC4 — re-measure the live overshoot: `[non-codebase]`, satisfied by substitute.** The live condition this criterion asks to re-measure **no longer exists**: the operator pruned that build cache at approximately 10:55 UTC on 2026-09-05 while relieving disk pressure, unrelated to this fix. The BuildKit cache reads 0 now, so the 5.875 GB against a 5.00 GiB budget cannot be re-measured by anyone, and this agent is in any case barred from mutating the production host.

The criterion is tagged `[non-codebase]` because its evidence is a **live host measurement**, which is inherently outside the repository snapshot a completion verifier reads — not because the codebase merely fails to show it. The substitute is arguably stronger than what AC4 asked for: `pct_of_cap 5875000000 5368709120` -> **109**, asserted in `test_a_cap_overrun_publishes_the_true_ratio_not_a_ceiling` at the exact bytes measured live on 2026-09-05. It is reproducible on every CI run, where the host state is gone for good. The ratio the metric now publishes IS `docker system df` divided by `builder.gc.maxUsedSpace`, computed by the shipped function on the recorded inputs.

Someone with host access should confirm on the next natural overshoot; nothing blocks on it, and the arithmetic is pinned either way.

**AC5 — portability: MET.** Pure shell arithmetic; the tests are local pytest driving `bash` over PATH stubs, with no AWS, Docker, systemd or CI-provider trigger. The `[non-codebase]` criterion above is the only one whose evidence is not reproducible from the repository.

## Verification run

81 tests pass across the five observability files plus `test_alarm_actions_terraform.py`, re-run after rebasing onto current `main`. `make lint` green. `make verify` ran on the pre-rebase tree and reported 29 failures — **26 of them `GateCongestedError: gate admission refused: all 4 concurrent slots`**, a shared host-level admission semaphore saturated by other work on the box, with **zero failures in any file this change touches**; re-run serially, 20 of 21 passed and the last failed with a different error that passes when its file runs alone (cross-test contamination). CI's `Verified +1` on 2679 is the authoritative signal and it is green.

## Scope note preserved

This is NOT `regretful-enormous-horsefly` (`docker_unaccounted_bytes` differencing allocated blocks against apparent size). That one produces a wrong NUMBER from sound plumbing; this produced a CENSORED number from a deliberate clamp. The `clamped at 0` lower bound on `docker_unaccounted_bytes` at `observability.sh:259` is a different metric with different semantics and was deliberately left alone.

compiled_state.description:
## The defect

`pct_of_cap` in `infra/scripts/observability.sh:304-309` clamps its output:

    pct_of_cap() {
      local pct
      pct=$(( $1 * 100 / $2 ))
      [ "$pct" -gt 100 ] && pct=100
      printf '%s\n' "$pct"
    }

Three metrics are derived through it, and all three exist for exactly one purpose — to show whether a
storage cap is holding:

- `docker_storage_used_percent` (line 381, against `DOCKER_BUDGET_BYTES`)
- `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` (line 396, against `DOCKER_BUILDKIT_CACHE_BYTES`)
- `journal_used_percent` (line 487, against `JOURNAL_MAX_USE_BYTES`)

Because of the clamp, each is **structurally incapable of reporting the one condition it is deployed
to detect**. "Exactly at the cap" and "over the cap by any amount" are the same number. The metric
goes blind precisely when it starts to matter, and it does so silently — a clamped 100 looks like a
healthy pinned ceiling, not a breach.

> **Corrected during the fix: the affected set is FIVE call sites, not three.** The container
> writable layer (`container_writable_used_percent`, §2i) arrived with `8629e3874aea` while this
> ticket was being written, and `var_tmp_used_percent` (§2h, story `2ba3`) was already present and
> uncounted. The defect spreading by ordinary reuse of a shared helper is the argument for fixing
> the helper rather than the call sites, which is what landed.

## Live instance, measured

Measured on the production host 2026-09-05, `docker system df`:

    Build Cache   5.875 GB   104 entries   0 active

Configured cap, `builder.gc.maxUsedSpace` = **5.00 GiB = 5.368 GB**.

So the true ratio is **~109%**. The published `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` reads **100**.
The overshoot — roughly 0.5 GB, about 9% — is invisible in the metric, in its alarm, and in every
dashboard downstream of it.

The other two are not currently clamped only because they happen to be under their caps right now
(`docker_storage_used_percent` ~70, `journal_used_percent` flat at 57). They carry the identical
defect and will hide their own breach the moment one occurs.

## How this misled a live operator, concretely

I am an orchestrating session that has been reading these metrics all night. I repeatedly asserted —
on epic `endowed-upset-scaup` and on bug `cyclopean-bloodshot-hoatzin` — that "the BuildKit cap IS
working, and the number is bounded because something bounds it", citing the sustained 99-100%
reading as positive evidence of health. That inference was exactly backwards: the reading was pinned
because it was CLAMPED, over a cache that was actually 9% past its budget.

Worse, `rebar-docker-buildkit-cache-high` (threshold 85, GreaterThanThreshold) was in ALARM the whole
time and I discounted it as the cap doing its job. A clamped ceiling turns a firing alarm into
something an operator reads as reassurance. The mis-reading survived four separate measurement passes
and was only caught when an agent went to `docker system df` directly.

## Why clamping is the wrong call here, not merely lossy

Clamping a percentage is defensible for a gauge whose semantics stop at full — a progress bar, a disk
that physically cannot exceed its size. It is wrong for a BUDGET, where exceeding the number is not
an impossible state but the specific failure being watched for. `builder.gc.maxUsedSpace` is a
best-effort reclamation target, not a hard wall: BuildKit can and does sit above it. A budget metric
must be able to say 109.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `pct_of_cap` no longer clamps, so a value over the cap publishes its true ratio. Proven by a
      unit test driving the function with numerator > denominator and asserting the returned value
      is > 100, plus one at exactly the cap asserting 100.
- [x] The three call sites (docker storage, BuildKit cache, journal) publish unclamped values, and a
      test pins that each is derived through the unclamped path — so a future re-introduction of a
      clamp at any single site is caught.
- [x] The change is checked against every consumer of the three metrics before landing: the
      CloudWatch alarms in `monitoring_autodeploy.tf` and any dashboard or doc that assumes a 0-100
      range. State explicitly whether any alarm threshold or unit needs adjusting, or why none does.
      A metric that can now exceed 100 must not break an alarm that previously could not see it.
- [x] [non-codebase] The live BuildKit overshoot is re-measured after the fix and the published
      percentage is shown to match `docker system df` divided by `builder.gc.maxUsedSpace` — i.e.
      the metric reports the real ratio, not 100.
      provenance: environment=aws-ec2 i-00880b2c7f13527c5 (production Gerrit host); principal=overnight orchestrator session via SSM; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=simulation — the PRE-fix overshoot was measured live on that host (docker system df: Build Cache 5.875 GB against builder.gc.maxUsedSpace 5.00 GiB = 5.368 GB, ~109%, published as 100). The POST-fix live re-measurement was NOT performed: the same session pruned that cache at ~10:55 UTC while relieving disk pressure, removing the condition. The substitute is a unit test at those exact bytes, pct_of_cap 5875000000 5368709120 -> 109, which is reproducible where the host state no longer is.
- [x] Portability: pure shell arithmetic and local tests; no CI-provider trigger.

**On the `[non-codebase]` tag.** This criterion's evidence is a LIVE HOST MEASUREMENT, which is
inherently outside the repository snapshot a completion verifier reads — that is what the tag is
for, and it is not a case of the codebase merely failing to show something it could show. The live
condition itself no longer exists: the operator pruned that build cache at approximately 10:55 UTC
on 2026-09-05 while relieving disk pressure, unrelated to this fix, so the 5.875 GB against a
5.00 GiB budget cannot be re-measured by anyone. The substitute is
`pct_of_cap 5875000000 5368709120` -> **109**, asserted in
`test_a_cap_overrun_publishes_the_true_ratio_not_a_ceiling` at the exact bytes measured live, and
reproducible on every CI run where the host state is gone for good. Full evidence in the comments.

## Testing

1. RED first: assert `pct_of_cap 5875000000 5368709120` returns a value greater than 100. On current
   main this returns exactly 100 and the test fails for the right reason.
2. Boundary: at exactly the cap the function still returns 100 (no off-by-one introduced).
3. Consumer sweep: grep every reference to the three metric names across `infra/`, `docs/` and the
   terraform tree, and record the disposition of each.
4. Mutation: re-introduce the clamp at one of the three call sites and confirm at least one test
   turns RED.

## Scope note

This is NOT the same defect as `regretful-enormous-horsefly`, which concerns `docker_unaccounted_bytes`
differencing allocated-blocks against apparent-size. That one produces a wrong NUMBER from sound
plumbing; this one produces a CENSORED number from a deliberate clamp. They are independent and both
live.
